log.thought: Thought: Starting with a standard, well-regularized baseline configuration (moderate depth, moderate learning rate).
Thought: Testing a shallower tree (depth 3) with higher regularization and slightly smaller learning rate to prevent overfitting on the imbalanced 7% positive target.

Thought: Shallower depth 3 significantly improved PR-AUC to 0.3895. Now testing depth 2 with moderate-high regularization and 300 estimators to see if very simple additive stumps/interactions perform even better.
Thought: Depth 2 was slightly worse than depth 3 (0.373 vs 0.3895). Let's test depth 5 with high min_child_weight and strong regularization to see if deeper interactions help or cause overfitting.
Thought: Depth 5 with high min_child_weight (7) and strong regularization achieved 0.3996. Let's explore depth 6 with min_child_weight=8 and strong L2/L1 regularization.
Thought: Depth 6 was 0.3967, close to depth 5's 0.3996. Now testing depth 4 with similar high min_child_weight (6) and low learning rate to complete the depth sweep around the sweet spot (4, 5, 6).
Thought: Depth 5 appears optimal. Let's refine around trial 4 by testing min_child_weight=8, slight feature subsampling (0.65), and subsample 0.75 with slightly more trees (220).
Thought: Comparing with Trial 4 (0.3996), isolate the effect of min_child_weight by testing min_child_weight=6 while keeping all other parameters identical to Trial 4.
Thought: min_child_weight=6 improved over 7 (0.4025 vs 0.3996). Testing min_child_weight=5 with all other parameters identical to see if the trend continues.
Thought: min_child_weight=6 is clearly best for depth 5. Now varying colsample_bytree to 0.8 (keeping subsample=0.7, min_child_weight=6, lr=0.02, n_estimators=200, lambda=4, alpha=0.1).
Thought: colsample_bytree=0.7 (0.4025) beats 0.8 (0.4015). Now testing colsample_bytree=0.6 to see if lower feature subsampling is even better.
Thought: colsample_bytree=0.7 is the sweet spot. Now testing subsample=0.8 (keeping colsample=0.7, max_depth=5, min_child_weight=6, lr=0.02, n_estimators=200, lambda=4, alpha=0.1).
Thought: subsample=0.8 degraded performance to 0.3953. Testing subsample=0.6 to test if lower subsampling helps.
Thought: subsample=0.7 and colsample=0.7 are established as strong values. Now investigating L2 regularization by varying reg_lambda from 4.0 to 3.0.
Thought: Decreasing lambda to 3.0 decreased performance (0.3948 vs 0.4025). Testing higher L2 regularization: reg_lambda=5.0.
Thought: reg_lambda=4.0 gives 0.4025 and 5.0 gives 0.4020. Testing reg_lambda=4.5 in between them.
Thought: reg_lambda=4.0 is optimal. Now testing L1 regularization: increasing reg_alpha from 0.1 to 0.2.
Thought: Increasing reg_alpha to 0.2 produced our best score yet (0.4065). Testing reg_alpha=0.3.
Thought: reg_alpha=0.2 yielded 0.4065 while 0.1 was 0.4025 and 0.3 was 0.4032. Testing reg_alpha=0.15 to see if the peak lies between 0.1 and 0.2.
Thought: Testing reg_alpha=0.25 to see if the peak lies between 0.20 and 0.30.
Thought: In Trial 17 (0.4065), learning rate was 0.02 with 200 trees. Let's test n_estimators=180 to see if 200 trees had begun to slightly overfit.
Thought: 180 estimators gave 0.4050, lower than 200 (0.4065). Let's test n_estimators=220 to see if slightly more trees help.
Thought: n_estimators=200 is optimal for lr=0.02. Now exploring a slightly lower learning rate (0.015) with proportionately more trees (260) to see if fine-grained steps improve PR-AUC.
Thought: Testing slightly faster learning rate: lr=0.025 with 160 trees on the best configuration so far.
Thought: Testing colsample_bytree=0.75 on top of Trial 17 (alpha=0.2, lambda=4, lr=0.02, depth=5, min_child_weight=6, subsample=0.7).

Thought: In Trial 4, min_child_weight=7 gave 0.3996 when alpha was 0.1. Now testing min_child_weight=7 with the optimal alpha=0.2 (keeping lambda=4.0, lr=0.02, depth=5, colsample=0.7, subsample=0.7, n_estimators=200).
Thought: Testing min_child_weight=5 with alpha=0.2 (holding lambda=4.0, lr=0.02, depth=5, colsample=0.7, subsample=0.7, n_estimators=200).
Thought: Testing reg_lambda=4.5 with alpha=0.2 (holding all other parameters at Trial 17's best).
Thought: reg_lambda=4.5 was 0.4064, nearly identical to reg_lambda=4.0 at 0.4065. Fine-tuning reg_alpha around 0.2: testing reg_alpha=0.18 with reg_lambda=4.0.
Thought: Testing reg_alpha=0.22 with all other parameters identical to Trial 17 to check if the peak is slightly above 0.20.
